incidents.vector: Attackers chained two zero-days in SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances (CVE-2026-15409, a max-severity SSRF, and CVE-2026-15410, an authenticated command injection) to gain unauthenticated remote code execution and root access before a patch existed.
incidents.impact: A ransomware operator exploited the flaws from June 22 to breach multiple enterprise networks, steal credentials and session data, pivot to domain controllers, and in at least one case deploy ransomware; CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the servers of Japan's largest refrigerated logistics company, prompting it to disconnect key systems to contain the intrusion.
incidents.impact: The outage halted parts of Nichirei's network of 140 refrigerated distribution centers, disrupting deliveries to KFC Japan's 1,300+ restaurants, Kura Sushi, Aeon supermarkets and others; some servers held personal data and Japan's data authorities were notified.

incidents.victim: Software users in the U.S. and Europe
incidents.vector: The actor tracked as UAT-11795 used ClickFix social engineering and trojanized installers (MobaXterm, WebEx, Zoom, DBeaver, FACEIT) to deploy a Python-based 'Starland RAT' and a bespoke PowerShell 'WLDR' C2 implant, with CastleStealer and Remcos as follow-on payloads.
incidents.impact: The campaign, active since at least June 2025, steals victim credentials and cryptocurrency wallet assets and establishes persistent C2 access, predominantly affecting U.S. victims plus Germany, Romania and Venezuela.

incidents.vector: An AI-agent-led attack gained initial access by feeding a malicious dataset to a pipeline that exposed a code-execution vulnerability, then pivoted to harvest cloud and cluster credentials.
incidents.impact: Hugging Face disclosed the breach and compromised credentials, urging users to rotate access tokens and review account activity; it said it has no evidence yet that user credentials were harvested.

incidents.vector: Russian state hackers scan the internet for exposed IP cameras, exploit weak or default credentials and outdated firmware, then use image-recognition software to analyze feeds for military vehicles and cargo.
incidents.impact: Dutch intelligence (AIVD/MIVD) warned that compromised cameras along military logistics routes in the Netherlands and beyond are used to track NATO weapons shipments to Ukraine; in Ukraine, hacked feeds have helped locate soldiers for lethal targeting.

incidents.vector: Threat actors actively exploited three SharePoint Server flaws (CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164) to achieve remote code execution, steal IIS machine keys and use deserialization techniques for persistence.
incidents.impact: CISA warned all supported on-premises SharePoint versions are affected and urged hardening, AMSI enablement and machine-key rotation; the SharePoint zero-day was among two actively exploited bugs in Microsoft's record 622-CVE July Patch Tuesday.

incidents.victim: AsyncAPI npm packages and downstream developers
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an unprotected pre-production release branch and a misconfigured GitHub Actions workflow to harvest CI/CD secrets, then used a stolen npm token to publish five trojanized @asyncapi packages that execute a Miasma RAT at import time via an IPFS-hosted second stage.
incidents.impact: The self-narrating loader affected developer workstations, CI/CD pipelines and container builds, with the RAT harvesting GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud and Kubernetes credentials via a highly resilient decentralized C2; Microsoft and Unit 42 urged immediate removal and credential rotation.

incidents.victim: Poland energy grid and water facilities
incidents.vector: Russia's FSB Center 16 conducted attempted cyber sabotage against Poland's energy sector and water treatment facilities, including a December 2025 attack on the power grid.
incidents.impact: The grid attack came 'very close' to causing a blackout that would have cut heating to half a million people in winter; the EU and UK responded with their first coordinated cyber sanctions against Russia, targeting 30+ individuals and entities, and France summoned the Russian ambassador.

incidents.industry: Multiple (energy, defense, communications, finance, healthcare, government)
incidents.vector: FSB Center 16 actors scan the internet for poorly configured routers, using default or weak SNMP community strings to command devices to copy and exfiltrate their configurations via TFTP, and occasionally exploit old Cisco and Smart Install flaws (e.g., CVE-2008-4128, CVE-2018-0171).
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from the U.S. and 12 allied nations warned of more than a decade of opportunistic compromise of critical infrastructure routers across multiple sectors, urging SNMPv3, disabling Smart Install and stronger credential hygiene.

incidents.vector: Threat actors using tradecraft associated with 'ShinyHunters' abused trusted OAuth relationships — via vishing that tricked staff into authorizing malicious connected apps, supply-chain compromises of Salesloft, Gainsight and Klue integrations, and misconfigured Salesforce guest/Aura access.
incidents.impact: The campaigns enabled quiet enumeration and mass exfiltration of CRM records (accounts, contacts, case data) at scale across many tenants while evading authentication-based detections; Microsoft worked with Salesforce to add near-real-time OAuth telemetry.

incidents.victim: U.S. businesses, hospitals and municipal governments
incidents.vector: OFAC and the UK sanctioned First VPN Service (1VPNS) and its administrator for selling anonymity infrastructure to ransomware operators, plus an individual selling 'cryptors' used to disguise malware from security tools.
incidents.impact: Numerous ransomware groups used 1VPNS infrastructure to hide attack origins, deploy malware and manage exfiltrated data against U.S. businesses, financial firms, hospitals and municipalities, causing billions in losses; the action followed a May 2026 European law-enforcement takedown.

incidents.vector: The RaaS operation tracked as 'The Gentlemen' uses edge-device exploitation, brute force, stolen credentials and initial access brokers, plus a custom Go backdoor, an EDR-killer framework and a suspected zero-day to disable defenses.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 counted 580 claimed victims since inception, with June 2026 its highest month (117 victims) — roughly a 6x increase over late 2025 — making it the second most active RaaS program of 2026, aided by an unusually generous 90% affiliate payout.

incidents.victim: Latvijas Valsts Mezi (LVM, Latvian state forestry company)
incidents.vector: A financially motivated ransomware group exploited a vulnerability in a system that had not been updated for two years and dwelled in the network for more than a week before detection.
incidents.impact: The attack knocked LVM's mapping, hunting and contractor systems offline (two-thirds of contract customers still lacked access weeks later) and leaked ~44 GB of stolen data including credentials, code and cryptographic keys; the same actor also breached pharma firm Olpha. Latvia's election infrastructure was confirmed unaffected.

incidents.vector: A large-scale campaign scans websites and exploits a broad list of known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (WordPress plugins, Craft CMS, Joomla JCE, MetInfo and others) enabling unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF or deserialization to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert warning that compromised web servers are used for defacement, credential capture, malware distribution and as a pathway to broader network compromise, with many Australian SMBs already impacted.

incidents.vector: A rebranded RaaS operation ('Hyadina') deployed a new 'GodDamn' locker using a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver attack, abusing a malicious kernel driver ('PoisonX') that carried a legitimate Microsoft Hardware Compatibility signature to kill security software, alongside 14 open-source credential-theft tools.
incidents.impact: Symantec observed the group entrenching in an unnamed victim via signed drivers, commercial RMM software and PsExec lateral movement before deploying ransomware, highlighting the risk of Microsoft-signed malicious drivers.

incidents.victim: Organizations hit by destructive wiping activity
incidents.vector: Microsoft analyzed 'GigaWiper', a Golang backdoor combining C2 capabilities with multiple destructive payloads — physical-disk wiping, fake ransomware derived from Crucio (unrecoverable encryption), and a FlockWiper reimplementation with multi-pass secure wiping.
incidents.impact: First observed in October 2025, the modular implant consolidates several destructive tools into on-demand backdoor commands to overwrite raw disks and remove partition metadata, reflecting a shift toward efficient, deployable wiper platforms.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in third-party software used by an email platform KDDI operates for five Japanese internet service providers.
incidents.impact: The breach exposed more than 12.2 million customer email addresses and 7.6 million passwords; KDDI patched the flaw, forced password resets and said its own consumer email services on separate infrastructure were unaffected.

incidents.victim: Unpatched edge routers and IoT devices (ORB network)
incidents.vector: The China-nexus actor UAT-7810 exploits known n-day flaws in unpatched Ruckus wireless routers (and ASUS AiCloud routers) to build the LapDogs Operational Relay Box network, deploying new custom backdoors tracked as LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH and JARLEASH.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos reports the actor continues expanding covert relay infrastructure that secondary China-nexus groups (such as UAT-5918) use to proxy espionage attacks against high-value targets while blending into legitimate traffic.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — AI-agent ransomware, financially motivated
incidents.vector: An 'agentic threat actor' (tracked as JadePuffer) exploited a Langflow RCE flaw (CVE-2025-3248) then pivoted to a production server running MySQL and Alibaba Nacos, with an LLM autonomously driving reconnaissance, credential theft, lateral movement, encryption and destruction.
incidents.impact: Sysdig documented the first end-to-end LLM-run ransomware operation: the agent enumerated and exfiltrated the database, deleted it, and left an extortion note, running 600+ payloads and fixing a failed step in 31 seconds — signaling the skill floor for ransomware has dropped sharply.

incidents.victim: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway operators
incidents.vector: Attackers began exploiting CVE-2026-8451, a memory-overread flaw in NetScaler devices configured as a SAML identity provider, within 24 hours of a public proof-of-concept, using a payload that floods the XML parser to read past the buffer boundary.
incidents.impact: Reminiscent of the CitrixBleed flaw, the vulnerability leaks sensitive memory that can enable initial access, privilege escalation, lateral movement and data exfiltration; researchers observed a coordinated scanning-and-exploitation campaign and urged immediate patching.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — botnet and proxy operator
incidents.vector: The FBI and industry partners seized hundreds of domains tied to NetNut, a residential proxy service run by Israeli firm Alarum Technologies that populated the Popa botnet by turning smart TVs and streaming boxes into always-on proxy nodes with little or no user consent.
incidents.impact: The seized network of at least two million compromised devices was rented out to relay abusive traffic including mass scraping, advertising fraud and account-takeover activity; the FBI and IRS replaced NetNut's homepage with a seizure notice.

incidents.vector: An attack attributed to the 'Cyber Isnaad Front' targeted an Israeli industrial refrigeration system, programming it to fail in a way requiring expertise in both Windows internals and refrigerant physics.
incidents.impact: Recorded Future's Insikt Group cited the sabotage as evidence that IRGC-backed personas, increasingly aided by AI for reconnaissance, are focused on disrupting adversaries' supply chains, logistics, industrial operations and food production.
